themes_detail.label: Tree Emergency & Green Space Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Crown Heights residents filed 6 new tree requests THIS WEEK (vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks)—a 2,300% spike—while simultaneously reporting 5 overgrown tree/branch complaints (900% above baseline), suggesting either a sudden storm event, neglected maintenance, or coordinated community push for green infrastructure that warrants investigation.
evidence: New Tree Requests: 6 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
Overgrown Tree/Branches: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.36)
Both spikes emerged simultaneously this week, suggesting a triggering event or coordinated action
reporting_angles: Did a recent storm damage or expose overgrown trees across the district?
Is this a coordinated community board or activist push for street tree expansion in an under-canopied neighborhood?

themes_detail.label: Facilities & Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance and facility complaints jumped to 22 THIS WEEK (340% above the 5.0 weekly average), and elevator complaints spiked 700% to 3 complaints, suggesting systemic issues in building infrastructure or park facilities that may affect multiple buildings or public spaces.
evidence: Maintenance or Facility complaints: 22 THIS WEEK vs. 5.0 weekly average (z-score: 8.01)
Elevator complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
Combined spike suggests broad infrastructure strain affecting residential buildings
reporting_angles: Are older multi-family buildings in Crown Heights facing a wave of elevator failures or deferred maintenance?
What public facilities (parks, libraries, community centers) are driving the spike in maintenance complaints?

themes_detail.label: Homelessness Visibility & Services Pressure
themes_detail.summary: Homeless Person Assistance complaints surged to 26 complaints 3 weeks ago (670% above the 3.4 weekly average, z-score 13.68)—the highest spike in the dataset—indicating either a visible encampment crisis or urgent unmet service needs in the district.
evidence: Homeless Person Assistance complaints: 26 (3 weeks ago) vs. 3.4 weekly average (z-score: 13.68, highest in dataset)
Community Board has standing budget request for 'Other facilities for homeless' (repeated annually, indicating chronic unmet need)
Spike predates current week but remains most statistically anomalous signal in data
reporting_angles: What triggered the 26-complaint spike 3 weeks ago—a new encampment, service closure, or seasonal factor?
Why does the Community Board repeatedly request expanded homeless services, and what gaps exist in current DHS capacity?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles & Street Blight
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints jumped to 17 last week (178% above the 6.1 weekly average, z-score 4.81), suggesting a recent surge in vehicle abandonment or towing delays that contributes to street disorder and may correlate with broader disinvestment.
evidence: Abandoned Vehicle complaints: 17 last week vs. 6.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.81)
Represents 178% increase from baseline, sustained into current week
Complements chronic illegal parking problem (2,284 complaints over 90 days, #1 category)
reporting_angles: Is NYPD/DSNY towing capacity overwhelmed, or are residents abandoning vehicles due to economic strain?
Do specific blocks or parking-constrained areas show clustering of abandoned vehicles?

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Decay & Navigation Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints hit 3 about 2 weeks ago (700% above the 0.4 weekly average), a sharp but narrower spike suggesting localized infrastructure vandalism or maintenance gap affecting wayfinding and delivery accessibility.
evidence: Street Sign - Missing complaints: 3 (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
700% spike but lower absolute volume than other infrastructure issues
Suggests localized rather than district-wide problem
reporting_angles: Which intersections or blocks are missing signs, and is this due to vandalism or maintenance backlog?
Does sign loss create navigation hazards for seniors, delivery workers, or people with visual impairments?
